author: StarTalk
description:
Make it yourself at lovable.com

Are there habitable worlds that look nothing like Earth? Neil deGrasse Tyson and comic co-host Matt Kirshen discuss NASA’s Habitable Worlds Observatory and its eventual search for life beyond our solar system with astrophysicist Evgenya Shkolnik.

Learn about SPARCS, a backpack-sized, 9-centimeter CubeSat telescope that studies the ultraviolet light of stars known to host planets. How did we go from zero known exoplanets to data showing the average star has at least one? What does “habitable” really mean? 

They break down the Goldilocks zone, why water must actually be present, and why habitable doesn’t mean inhabited. Is it bias to look for Earth-like life? They discuss biosignatures, extremophiles, and why we start with what we know. 

We explore the Habitable Worlds Observatory. You’ll learn about what instruments are planned and how those tools will help us locate habitable worlds and more. We discuss how UV light can erode atmospheres or fake bio
title: The New NASA Mission to Find Life in the Universe, with Evgenya Shkolnik
